rationale: PINS `decorates` FROM DECLARATION-POSITION TEMPLATE HASKELL SPLICES — the construct that makes this label implementable in a language whose attributes are otherwise passive metadata. Template Haskell runs code at COMPILE TIME: `$(makeLenses ''Widget)` applies the function `makeLenses` to the named declaration `Widget`, and `makeLenses` GENERATES accessor declarations for it, so the declaration carries a decorator in the vocabulary's sense (`decorates`: a decorator is applied to a declaration). THE DISCRIMINATOR IS THE QUOTED DECLARATION, NEVER THE HEAD: TH decorators are LIBRARY functions (`makeLenses` from Control.Lens.TH, `deriveJSON` from Data.Aeson.TH) — requiring the head to be declared in-file would exclude the construct — so the test is a `th_quoted_name` argument naming a declaration THIS file declares. Both splice forms parse as `top_splice` (grammar-confirmed before this file was written): `$(makeLenses ''Widget)` is top_splice -> splice -> parens -> apply(variable, th_quoted_name), and the bare `makePrisms ''Gadget` is top_splice -> apply. THE DIRECTION: source = the enclosing module scope, target = the decorated DECLARATION's own symbol; the decorator name is external and unresolvable, so it rides in `metadata.decoratorName` and NO edge is emitted to it (an edge to a name nothing declares is a claim the index cannot answer). FIRE: (1) module scope -> Widget, decoratorName makeLenses, line 57; (2) module scope -> Gadget, decoratorName makePrisms, line 60. FORBID, each the failure the discriminator could plausibly make: (A) a plain application `makeLenses n` in a function body is an `apply`, not a declaration splice — no decorates from `compute`; (B) `$(makeLenses ''ForeignRecord)` quotes a declaration this file does NOT declare — no decorates whose target is ForeignRecord, because this file cannot own that declaration; (C) `$(do pure [])` is a declaration-position splice with NO callable head (a generator) — no decorates at all beyond the two fire rows, pinned by an exact count; (D) `INSTANCE_CLUMP_1(Widget)` is a C-preprocessor macro line the grammar parses as a bare top-level expression splice — callable-shaped head, no quoted declaration, no decorates. The exact count (2) is the pin that keeps C and D silent, and the forbid rows name B and A by their own endpoints so a regression cannot hide behind the count.

expectRelationships.comment: FIRE 1 — the $( ... ) form. Source is the module scope, target is the DECORATED declaration, and the imported decorator's name is metadata rather than a dangling endpoint.
FIRE 2 — the BARE declaration form `makePrisms ''Gadget` (no `$`), which parses as top_splice -> apply. Pinning both forms keeps the rule from depending on the dollar spelling.

expectRelationshipCount.comment: EXACTLY the two fire rows. This is the pin that keeps FORBID (C) `$(do pure [])` and FORBID (D) the CPP-macro splice silent: neither has a quoted declaration, so neither may add a row. It also keeps a future over-eager rule (one that fires on every splice) from passing on the two positive rows alone.

forbidRelationships.comment: FORBID (A) — `compute n = makeLenses n` is a plain APPLICATION of the same TH function to a VALUE. It is an apply node inside a function body, not a declaration-position top_splice, so it is not a decoration. A rule keyed on the decorator NAME instead of the node type would emit this.

FORBID (B) — `$(makeLenses ''ForeignRecord)` quotes a declaration this file does NOT declare. The quoted name must resolve against THIS file's module-scope declarations; a row here would source an edge from a declaration the file does not own.
the decorator is EXTERNAL. An edge to it would assert a target nothing in this file declares — the claim the index cannot answer. The name belongs in metadata.decoratorName.
as above, for the bare-form decorator
FORBID (C) — `$(do pure [])` runs at compile time but applies no callable to a named declaration. `pure` is a head inside a do block, not a decorator applied to a declaration.
